claims.text: The local source slice models two ANA Everyone's Happy Campaign phase 2 rows: Moltres row 121 and Zapdos row 122.

Bulbapedia's Moltres and Zapdos card pages say the second ANA Everyone's Happy Campaign phase ran between August 1 and September 30, 1999, and passengers could redeem two domestic boarding-pass stubs for the two-card set.
Bulbapedia describes the same postcard-to-Media Factory redemption route for this phase: eligible domestic boarding-pass stubs were affixed to special postcards and mailed to Media Factory.
Bulbapedia credits the Japanese ANA Moltres and Zapdos artwork to Toshinao Aoki.

Bulbapedia notes that early English Wizards Promo Moltres and Zapdos cards credited Toshinao Aoki, while a later English print corrected the artist credit to Naoyo Kimura. That credit history is English-route context, not a reason to overwrite the Japanese ANA Aoki credit.

This source group matters because phase 2 turns the ANA campaign into a legendary-bird route: after phase 1's Articuno, the second campaign window supplies Moltres and Zapdos through the same flight-evidence redemption mechanics.

Agents should preserve ANA Everyone's Happy Campaign phase 2 route, August 1-September 30 1999 date window, rows 121-122 pair identity, two domestic boarding-pass stub redemption, special postcard / Media Factory mechanics, Toshinao Aoki Japanese-art context, English Aoki/Kimura credit boundary, and non-equivalence with ANA phase 1, ANA Get in a Jet, Wizards Black Star, Pokemon Web, Supreme Victors, Beat of the Frontier, and later legendary-bird memories before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: ANA Everyone's Happy Campaign phase 2 — the bird route completes its flight
narrative.why_it_matters: Phase 2 is where the ANA campaign starts to feel like a collector's flight path instead of a one-off novelty. Articuno had already made phase 1 feel airborne; Moltres and Zapdos arrive through the second campaign window and make the legendary-bird assembly whole. The identity is not just 'Japanese promo bird.' It is August and September 1999, two domestic boarding-pass stubs, a postcard, Media Factory, and Aoki's connected sky imagery. That route matters because these birds keep slipping into nearby memories: English Wizards promos, Pokemon Web, Supreme Victors, Beat of the Frontier, and later legendary-bird nostalgia. The agent has to keep the flight record attached.

narrative.human_title: Moltres — the fire bird on an airline route
narrative.why_it_matters: Moltres is the warmer half of phase 2's ANA bird pair. What makes it sing is not only the legendary name, but the strange physical path: passengers flew domestic routes, saved boarding-pass stubs, sent postcards to Media Factory, and received a card whose whole identity is now inseparable from flight. For an agent, the danger is obvious. Moltres appears again and again in Wizards, Pokemon Web, Supreme Victors, Beat of the Frontier, and later legendary-bird memory. The ANA route has to stay attached.

narrative.human_title: Zapdos — the electric bird with a flight record
narrative.why_it_matters: Zapdos is the card that makes phase 2 crackle. It is a legendary bird, yes, but in this catalogue the why is stranger and better: the owner once had to pass through an airline campaign route, with boarding-pass stubs and a postcard standing between ordinary travel and a Pokemon card. For agents, the beauty and the risk are the same. Zapdos is famous enough to attract lazy matches. The ANA phase, Aoki credit, Japanese name, and English-credit caveat keep the card from being smeared into generic legendary-bird memory.
